chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan, from Ayyūb ibn Nūḥ, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Manṣūr ibn Ḥāzim, from ʿAnbasah ibn Muṣʿab, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The leftover water of the menstruating woman may be drunk from, but wudu (ablution) is not performed with it.

key_terms.سُؤْرُ: leftover water or drink remaining after someone has used it

ai.seo_question: Can one drink from the leftover water of a menstruating woman, and can it be used for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the leftover water of a menstruating woman. It states that such water is permissible to drink, while wudu (ablution) is not to be performed with it, indicating a distinction between drinking and ritual use.
